clue.text: Sleep and oxygen helping recovery

parts.note: sleep is a kind of rest
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
a helping is a portion or ration of food

explanation.surface: A recipe for getting well: plenty of sleep, fresh air and good food.
explanation.definitionFit: Restoring something to health or good condition is its recovery, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Worked miracle to effect recapture

indicators.note: worked suggests the word miracle is kneaded into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone performs a miracle to win something back.
explanation.definitionFit: To claim back what was lost is to recover or retake it.

clue.text: Dawn is a big star at university

parts.note: the sun is a large star
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A celebrated student famous on campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunrise, the moment the sun appears above the horizon, is dawn.

clue.text: Authority to sink graves, say, on the premises?

definitions.text: Authority to sink graves, say, on the premises?

parts.words: Authority to sink graves, say, on the premises?
parts.note: reads like a gravedigger's permit, but Graves is a Bordeaux wine and sinking it means drinking it in a bar

explanation.surface: Permission to dig graves on a property.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is a licence to sell alcohol for drinking where it is bought, as in a pub, unlike an off-licence shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A permit allowing alcohol to be consumed where sold is exactly a drinking authority on the premises.

clue.text: A mile approved? Crazy people run it!

parts.note: OK means approved

explanation.surface: Is a mile run acceptable? Only madmen would run one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes the phrase 'run amok', to rush about wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: People in a frenzy are said to run wild in this way, a fixed idiom.

clue.text: Tip diner managed for game?

indicators.note: managed suggests the words are handled and arranged anew

explanation.surface: A restaurant tip arranged for a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' is the adjective meaning plucky, ready for anything; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A game person is plucky and willing, the same as someone fearless.

clue.text: Original story

explanation.surface: A tale never told before.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means new or original; as a noun, a book-length fictional narrative.

clue.text: Second teams announced also

indicators.note: announced means the phrase is taken by its sound when said out

parts.note: B sides are second-string teams, a usage from sport

explanation.surface: Reserve sides were named in the line-up as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides means in addition, a synonym of also.

clue.text: Bruiser who uses a drumstick?

explanation.surface: A thug who plays the drums.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruiser is one who batters people; a drummer beats or batters a drum with a stick.

clue.text: Lock-opening craft?

parts.note: reads like the skill of a burglar picking locks, but means a vessel that passes through the locks of a waterway

explanation.surface: A burglar's skill at picking locks.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrowboat on a waterway has gates opened for it at each lock it passes through.

clue.text: Almost lavish, in a way, opening such bottles?

indicators.note: in a way suggests the remaining letters are arranged in some other fashion
almost means the word lavish stops short of its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone extravagantly opening a stock of small bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter of lavish to leave LAVIS, and 'in a way' rearranges those letters; 'opening' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Small glass containers for medicine or perfume are a kind of bottle.

clue.text: Scene in opera spectacular

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words opera spectacular, across the gap

explanation.surface: A view of a lavish operatic production.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is a view or outlook, much as a scene is what lies before the eye.

clue.text: Voided contract to secure rooms

indicators.note: to secure means the contract word holds the rooms word fast inside it

parts.note: a deed is a legal contract
a flat is a set of rooms

explanation.surface: A tenancy agreement cancelled while trying to get a place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deflated has had its air let out, so it is emptied or voided.

clue.text: First service?

parts.note: looks like a tennis serve or first course, but means the earliest of the day's church offices

explanation.surface: Who serves first in a match?
explanation.definitionFit: Morning prayer is the first of the canonical hours of the church day.

clue.text: Asking for a loan of money can be heartbreaking

definitions.text: Asking for a loan of money

explanation.surface: Begging a loan can be moving.
explanation.walkthrough: To touch someone is slang for asking them for money; 'can be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapping someone for cash is slangily touching them; moving or poignant is the other sense.

clue.text: Terminals in which parrot is suspect?

indicators.note: suspect suggests the words are dubious and need putting into a different order

explanation.surface: A suspicious parrot detained at an air terminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges PARROT IS; 'in which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Air terminals are the buildings and fields where flights arrive and depart.

clue.text: Christmas show which top men aim to turn out

indicators.note: turn out suggests the words are turned around into a new form

explanation.surface: The festive production that leading men hope to stage.
explanation.walkthrough: A PANTOMIME is a British family Christmas stage show with farce and audience participation; 'which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Panto is the traditional British seasonal theatre entertainment staged around Christmas.

clue.text: Uncle's place of business-or Pop's, would you say?

explanation.surface: Is the family business uncle's or Dad's?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker, and to pop something is to pawn it, so a 'Pop's' is where you pop things.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle is slang for the moneylender who takes goods in pledge, and popping is slang for pledging them.

clue.text: Doctor is a poet reading aloud

indicators.note: reading aloud means the poet's name is taken by how it is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: A. E. Housman was an English poet, author of A Shropshire Lad

explanation.surface: A medic who gives poetry readings.
explanation.walkthrough: HOUSEMAN is the British term for a junior hospital doctor; it sounds like HOUSMAN, the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a houseman is a junior hospital doctor in their first year.

clue.text: Tries over a year to obtain report

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case

explanation.surface: A court spends a year getting to the bottom of an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearsay is information reported second-hand, rumour.

clue.text: A National Trust border county?

parts.note: NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust, the British heritage charity
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Does the heritage charity own a county on the border?
explanation.walkthrough: ANTRIM is a county of Northern Ireland, which borders the Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is one of the six traditional counties of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Doctor to charge when nightlight is lost

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
an onset is an attack or charge

explanation.surface: A doctor billing patients after a power cut.
explanation.definitionFit: When the moon goes below the horizon its light disappears from the night sky.

clue.text: Tenacious advocate

explanation.surface: A dogged champion of a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means sticking fast, tenacious; as a noun, a follower or supporter of a cause.

clue.text: Run over, harness-horse is retired

indicators.note: retired suggests the horse withdrawing, going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a pacer is a horse trained for harness racing

explanation.surface: A trotting horse knocked down and put out to grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To summarise again, going back over the main points, is a recap.

clue.text: Blanket found in mountain top on Choctaw? No further south

indicators.note: found in shows the letters lie inside the run mountain top on Choctaw

explanation.surface: A blanket discovered on a peak in Choctaw country.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'top on Choctaw'. 'No further south' hints that this cloak belongs to South America rather than to the North American Choctaw.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American cloak is essentially a blanket with a hole for the head.

clue.text: Ding-dong for the MacDonalds, say, at opening of Glencoe?

parts.note: the MacDonalds are an example of a Scottish clan

indicators.note: opening of points to the first letter of the word Glencoe

explanation.surface: A fight for the MacDonalds at the start of the Glencoe massacre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ding-dong' is a ringing noise, though it suggests a fight; Glencoe is the Highland glen where the MacDonalds were massacred in 1692. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is a loud ringing sound, like the ding-dong of a bell.

clue.text: Employer's quarter in ancient city

indicators.note: in shows the quarter word sitting within the city word

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia
SE, southeast, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: A boss's district in an old city.
explanation.definitionFit: One who uses something employs it.

clue.text: Coins may be changed in such a boom!

indicators.note: changed suggests the letters of the word coins are swapped round, like coins exchanged for others

explanation.surface: A loud bang from coins being exchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonic boom is the bang made by an aircraft passing the speed of sound.

clue.text: Hails spot to be developed for health installations

indicators.note: developed suggests the site is reworked, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A town welcomes a site being built up for clinics.
explanation.definitionFit: Places where the sick are treated are the main installations of a health service.

clue.text: Device to keep the work down in the office?

definitions.text: Device to keep the work down in the office?

parts.words: Device to keep the work down in the office?
parts.note: sounds like a way of limiting one's workload, but means an object that stops papers on a desk blowing away

explanation.surface: A trick for reducing one's workload at the office.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy desk object holds loose sheets in place so draughts cannot scatter them.
